criteria.name: answers_prompt
criteria.reason: The prompt asks for one root cause, but the essay names three: the filibuster ('filibustering has been used to bring democracy to a standstill'), 'inflexible ideologues', and 'Corrupt lobbying... veiled bribery'. It never says which one is the root.

criteria.name: specificity
criteria.reason: It has strong checkable detail: '90 percent of Americans', '74 percent of gun owners in the NRA', Harry Reid, cloture, TEFRA in September 1982, Tip O'Neill and Reagan. But the Manchin-Toomey vote was 54-46, not '55 to 45', and the amendment was bipartisan, not 'Obama's amendments'.

criteria.name: human_voice
criteria.reason: It reads like a person, but with stock framing: a rhetorical-question opener, 'Unfortunately', 'Of course', 'upper echelons', a not-because-X-but-because-Y line ('did not do so because of their passionate belief... but because'), about 8 em dashes and a subject-verb error ('Tools... has').

criteria.name: stories
criteria.reason: There are two on-topic case studies: the 2013 background-check vote and the 1982 TEFRA compromise. The first is muddled by the aside on Reid's 'lesser of two evils' choice, which weakens the essay's own argument.

criteria.name: ideas_mechanism
criteria.reason: It explains how the 60-vote cloture threshold lets a minority block a majority, and quotes Sinclair on why money shapes votes. But it then concedes Reid's route 'really was the lesser of two evils' and never connects the three causes into one.

criteria.name: structure_ending
criteria.reason: It opens on 'What happens to a democracy when the voice of the majority is no longer heard?' and ends on a borrowed JFK quote: 'Let us accept our own responsibility for the future.' The ending is a generic moral and never returns to the opening question.

fixes: Paragraph 1 (answers_prompt, about +12): commit to one root cause in a plain sentence, for example the 60-vote cloture rule that lets a Senate minority block what the majority wants. Cut 'This, coupled with a dangerous proliferation of inflexible ideologues'. Then rewrite the lobbying paragraph as the reason that rule gets abused, so it is no longer a second cause, or cut it.

Paragraph 2 (accuracy, recovers the -10): fix the facts before submitting. The Manchin-Toomey background-check amendment failed 54-46 on April 17, 2013, and it was a bipartisan Senate amendment, not 'Obama's amendments'. Change 'recent' to '2013'. Cut the 'perhaps this route really was the lesser of two evils' sentence, because it argues against your own thesis.

Voice and ending (about +8 plus the -6 recovered): remove all em dashes, change 'Tools... has' to 'have', and rewrite 'did not do so because of... but because' as a direct statement. Replace the JFK quote at the end with a closing line that answers the opening question, 'What happens to a democracy when the voice of the majority is no longer heard?', using the 54 senators from your own vote example.
